match.reason: The closest bank point, bus-operations-management, covers turning inputs into outputs but adds operations management, cost and quality aims, and says nothing about processes adding value, so it is broader than the new point and would need more than small changes.

draft.title: Inputs, processes and outputs
card: Operations is the part of a business that makes its goods or delivers its services. It turns inputs into outputs.
Inputs
the resources put into operations, such as materials, labour, equipment, energy and money.
Processes
the activities that change the inputs into outputs, such as cutting, assembling, cooking or advising a client. Good processes add value.
Outputs
the finished goods or services that go to customers. Value is added when the output is worth more to the customer than the inputs that went into it.
draft.remember: Inputs go in, processes change them, outputs come out worth more.

a.q: Which of these is a process in a furniture workshop?
opts: Sanding and assembling timber into chairs
Timber bought from a supplier
Finished chairs sent to a shop
The wages paid to the workers
a.why: Sanding and assembling are activities that change inputs into outputs. Timber is an input, and the finished chairs are outputs. Wages are money put in, so they are also an input.
a.clue: Look for the activity that changes one thing into another.

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Ballarat. She buys flour and butter, and her staff mix and bake them into loaves sold to customers. Which option correctly sorts these items?
opts: Flour is an input, baking is a process, loaves are outputs
Flour is a process, baking is an input, loaves are outputs
Flour is an input, baking is an output, loaves are a process
Flour and loaves are both inputs, baking is an output
b.why: Flour is a resource put in, so it is an input. Baking changes it, so it is a process. The loaves are what customers receive, so they are outputs. Baking is a tempting output only because it is the last step, but it is an activity, not the finished product.
b.clue: Ask what is put in, what is done to it, and what comes out.

a.best: Sanding and assembling timber into chairs

b.best: Flour is an input, baking is a process, loaves are outputs

problems.detail: The remember line says outputs 'come out worth more' without condition. The card says only that 'good processes add value' and that value is added 'when' the output is worth more, so not every output is worth more than its inputs. Suggest: 'Inputs go in, processes change them, outputs come out, and good processes add value.'

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, and each question has one clear right answer. The remember line overstates the card by implying that outputs are always worth more than their inputs.
